identity.title: Joint Learning in the Gaussian Single Index Model

problem.claim: Jointly learn a one-dimensional projection and a univariate function in a high-dimensional Gaussian single-index model.

contributions.claim: Analyzes gradient-flow dynamics for a natural alternating scheme and proves convergence with a rate governed by the function’s information exponent.
Shows that convergence can occur even when the initial direction is negatively correlated with the target direction.
Develops an RKHS-based implementation for efficient and flexible estimation of the univariate function.

stated_novelty.claim: The paper combines convergence analysis for joint projection–function learning, including negatively correlated initialization, with an RKHS implementation adapted to the model structure.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report a convergence proof for the alternating gradient-flow scheme, with rate controlled by the information exponent associated with Gaussian regularity.
The authors report convergence even from an initialization negatively correlated with the target direction.
The authors report that an adapted RKHS enables efficient and flexible estimation of the univariate function.

narrative_sequence.summary: Defines joint learning of a sphere-constrained projection and a univariate link function from Gaussian data.
Frames the setting as a non-convex problem connecting representation learning and nonlinear regression.
Studies an alternating gradient-flow scheme and gives a convergence rate tied to Gaussian regularity.
Reports convergence despite negative initial correlation with the target direction.
Uses an adapted RKHS to estimate the univariate function efficiently and flexibly.

source_observation.claim: The abstract links the convergence rate to an explicit function property—the information exponent reflecting Gaussian regularity.

lessons.interpretation: Making a rate depend on an identifiable structural quantity can explain variation in optimization behavior.
lessons.application: When presenting a theoretical rate, parameterize it by a clearly named regularity or information measure and state what aspect of the target it represents.
lessons.exception: This framing is unsuitable when the quantity is undefined, unestimable, or irrelevant to the intended setting.

source_observation.claim: The paper separately states a difficult-initialization result and an implementation choice adapted to the model’s low-dimensional structure.

lessons.interpretation: Pairing a robustness claim with a structure-matched computational realization connects theory to use conditions.
lessons.application: For a proposed learning method, analyze a challenging initialization regime and identify an estimator or representation aligned with the model’s intrinsic structure.
lessons.exception: Do not use this pairing when the application has no meaningful initialization issue or exploitable low-dimensional structure.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the assumptions, algorithmic details, definition of the information exponent, convergence metric, or rate formula.
No sample-complexity, runtime, numerical, baseline-comparison, or implementation details are reported.
The abstract does not establish priority or independently verify the stated proof and demonstrations.
